summary: Reconcile published scheduled and Run-now backups after interrupted retention under the original Core operation. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: After correcting repository access, the operator watches the original unresolved run settle rather than starting another backup for the same VM.

api.reason: No route or schema change. Core now retries settlement of an already-published scheduled or policy Run-now backup under its retained operation ID and reports the later result; Controller exact replay still returns its retained task.

roadmap.reason: Closes a recovery failure found in the existing destination interruption gate.

state.reason: No new durable record; Core already owns the run, metadata receipt, journal, catalog point and repository delete intent.

verification.method: A disposable S3 policy Run-now fault reached a durable delete intent and left the run needs_attention; after permission recovery and Core restart, exact Controller replay stayed needs_attention. The focused Core Run-loop regression reproduced a published point with write-denied retention before the retry path, then passed after Core reconciliation was added. It also covers scheduled recovery, terminal run with unfinished journal, and pre-canceled settlement. Focused race, SFTP stalled-handshake cancellation and serial full Go tests passed. Independent source review found a prune cancellation gap, then re-reviewed corrected context propagation without another concrete finding. Matched current-source Core autonomously settled the same S3 operation on restart before Controller; exact Controller replay reported success with no second run/point. A fresh SFTP permission fault then reached a durable delete intent and produced the same refusal/recovery sequence. Both old points pruned only after permission returned; both protected controls, original point/hash sets and source disk hashes remained intact.
verification.limits: These were controlled service permission refusals after durable intent, not abrupt power loss during a successful remote delete. Broader final-publication faults, mixed-version and forge CI remain open.
